doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Birth in New Orleans and early memories of music
summary: Born in 1912 in New Orleans, moved to Chicago at five; he recalls mostly the dixieland music, funeral parades and church.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: My birth date? I was born April the 11th, 1912, in New Orleans, Louisiana, and moved to Chicago when I was about five years old, then spent most of my life – my early life – in the Chicago area before moving to New York, which was much later in my life.
Let’s stay in New Orleans for a hot minute.
What are your early recollections of New Orleans?

The most things that stick closer to my mind is the music, because that was the era [of] dixieland music being played, the funeral parades, the church-going, and the social things that were happening in my family at that time, which really helped me to establish myself later on as a musician. The main thing was the music. I recall that more than anything else.
